title: AI Layoffs Don’t Add Up. Here’s the Data
summary: Recruiter digs into 2025 layoff data: AI is a small share of cuts, enterprise AI mostly stuck in pilots, juniors locked out.

assertions.quote: AI accounts for about 4.4% ... they blame any layoffs on AI transformation even when the real reasons are economic

verdicts.note: Analyses (e.g. Oxford Economics, Challenger data) find AI is a small share of cited layoff reasons and some 'AI' cuts track cost cutting; but some cuts do reflect real automation.

assertions.quote: Only about 30% of scaled AI beyond a few teams and only 39% report any bottom line impact

verdicts.note: McKinsey 2025 and the MIT NANDA report found most deployments in pilots and few with P&L impact; measurement methods vary and some sectors see clear returns.
There are reports of AI-motivated cuts being reversed (e.g. Klarna support staff) and analyst forecasts of rehiring, but broad 'boomerang' rehiring of engineers is weakly evidenced.

assertions.quote: The best AI could only complete 2 and a half% of those projects to professional standards

verdicts.note: The Remote Labor Index (Scale/CAIS, late 2025) found top agents completing ~2.5% of real Upwork-style projects acceptably; newer agents score higher but still low.

METR 2025 preliminary: agents often get the core functionality of real OSS issues right but fail to satisfy all requirements (docs, linting, tests). This points the same way for open-source issues, not freelance projects, and gives no rates.

assertions.quote: Graduate roles down 32% since Chat GBT launched

verdicts.note: Stanford 'Canaries' (2025) found ~13% relative employment decline for 22-25-year-olds in AI-exposed jobs, but rates, over-hiring correction and other macro factors also matter.

assertions.quote: No entry-level roles means no mid-level talent in five years

verdicts.note: A straightforward pipeline argument made by IBM and others; the long-run effect is unmeasured yet but well reasoned.

assertions.quote: can you verify AI output? Can you apply domain expertise to catch when it's wrong?

verdicts.note: Studies show novices accept incorrect AI code more often; verifying output requires domain and code literacy.
The review concludes that skill in verification, constraint specification and review may matter as much as authoring skill, and that the central risk is a verification gap.
